## Mitigation Checklist

When designing systems or managing access controls, apply these foundational practices:

### 1. Principle of Least Privilege
Grant write scope (and all permissions) only to the paths or resources a process genuinely needs. Do not assign broad or unconstrained access; start minimal and expand only when necessary. This limits damage if a process or credential is compromised.

### 2. Input Validation at Trust Boundaries
Treat all external content as untrusted data—never as instructions. Validate and sanitize all input at system boundaries before processing. This blocks injection attacks and ensures that data from external sources cannot modify program behavior unexpectedly.

### 3. Path Canonicalization
Resolve and validate file paths before any write operation to block directory traversal attacks. Canonicalize paths to their absolute form, check that they fall within approved scope, and reject any path that attempts to escape the allowed directory tree.

### 4. Audit Logging
Record every denied action with its reason for later review. Logs provide visibility into access attempts, security violations, and suspicious patterns—critical for incident response and forensics.
